notes: Candidates: the 8 tiles around the target (neighbors(): dc -1..1, then dr -1..1, on the board). A tile counts if it is empty (the sword itself ignored) and seamBlocks(tile, target) is false. seamBlocks only checks orthogonal neighbours, so a diagonal tile is never walled off. (towerLucifer.ts bladeLanding, neighbors; towerTerrain.ts seamBlocks)

Order (player and online-guest swords): the candidate with the smallest Manhattan distance from the sword wins. Ties go to the first in neighbors() order, because the comparison is strict '<'. (bladeLanding)

Order (demon AI swords): blockLanding() sorts candidates: first the tile one step from the target toward the AI's Lucifer, then tiles nearer Lucifer than the target is, then nearest Lucifer. The AI also prefers swords not standing in the gap between Lucifer and the target, then the sword nearest the landing tile. (blockLanding, launchDemonBlade)

Flask fallback: if no candidate is free and the target is soul-linked to a flask (contestLinked), the first neighbour holding a flask (contestBlocks) with no seam to the target is used. (bladeLanding)

Path: nothing on the way is checked. The sword flies a curved hop that bends away from the target (bladeFlightPoint) over bodies and earth lines. That bending is the 'swerve'; it's cosmetic, and only the landing tile matters.

No reachable tile: the foe isn't a target. bladeTargets() leaves it out, tapFreshBlade() returns false, no action is spent, the sword stays fresh, and there is nothing to refund because the summon card was already paid. The AI skips that foe and tries the next; if none works, no sword launches (launchDemonBlade returns null). The guest call returns false.
Landing tile taken by the time of the hit: the sword stays where it was, but the hit still lands for BLADE_AD. Afterwards its attack drops to BLADE_AD_AFTER. (towerLucifer.ts flies tick)
Cost: a player sword spends one action (chess.left, or focusLeft under a focus card). Guest and AI launches don't touch the action count. (tapFreshBlade, sendGuestBlade)

EA is asking DSK to switch the L33 default to true, so DSK's 'false' alternative is withdrawn.

behaviours.name: Terrain (what each tile id means)
behaviours.summary: The single home for tile meanings: for each logic tile id, whether units can stand, land or spawn there, whether landing kills, whether a push can enter, and whether it slows or trips. Edge walls (earth lines) are not tiles in the code: they sit on a tile's n/e/s/w edge and live in Barrier Line. Walls on tile edges (the map's logic.edges) always block movement and adjacency across that edge: that is core grid behaviour with no knob. The two wall knobs only decide whether walls also block line of sight and shots.
